headings.text: How the repository is laid out

blocks.html:
If you're working in this repository, start here, then jump to whichever guide fits what you're doing. The guides are deliberately short. The platform is still moving fast, and short docs are the ones that stay true.

Guide When to read
Architecture and playbook Read this first. It's the overall picture: the components, the deploy flow, and the two environments.
Development guide For running the platform locally or changing a manifest.
Integration guide For adding a new service, or wiring an existing one into the Deploy App platform.
Operating guide For building or deploying the cloud Zarf package, or running a live environment.

Getting started

Prerequisites

The repo pins tool versions through mise. Install mise first, then run the two setup commands from the repo root:

mise install        # installs the versions listed in mise.toml
mise trust          # trust the local mise.toml

Once mise is set up, kubectl, kind, helm, yq, task, and zarf all resolve to the pinned versions the moment you cd into the directory.

You'll also need Docker running, since kind spins up the cluster nodes as containers.

Without mise, install matching versions of kubectl 1.36, kind 0.31, helm 3, task 3, yq 4.53.2, and zarf 0.76.0 by hand. The pinned versions live in ../mise.toml.

Bring up the platform

From the repo root:

task up        # creates the kind cluster and runs all four deploy phases
task           # list every available task

task up is safe to run more than once. The kind cluster name and the port mappings come from ../kind-config.yaml, and ports 80, 443, plus the TAK and MediaMTX ports all bind to localhost.

When the deploy finishes, the UI is at https://localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi/. That hostname is just a public DNS record pointing at 127.0.0.1, so you don't need to touch /etc/hosts.

If task deploy dies partway through a phase, it's nearly always because a controller from the previous phase hasn't reported Ready yet. Run the same command again. The wait gates pick up where they left off.

Re-apply after editing
task deploy
task down      # deletes the kind cluster (alias for `cluster:delete`)

For the deeper local workflows (running mirrord against rmapi, working inside a service folder, rendering an overlay) see development.md.

What is "Rasenmaeher"?

Rasenmaeher is German for "lawn mower," which is why searching the name mostly turns up gardening equipment. It's the codename pvarki uses for the Deploy App: a platform that gives a team one login and one identity flow across a curated set of mission-critical services like TAK, Battlelog, MediaMTX, and Matrix. The original Docker Compose project lives at pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration. This repository is the Kubernetes / Kustomize port, and it's where the active work happens.

The compose-based upstream is deprecated now, so treat it as a reference for how things fit together rather than something to copy manifest by manifest.

How the repository is laid out

.
├── README.md            # Quick start
├── agents.md            # Working contract for code-editing agents
├── taskfile.yaml        # Lifecycle commands (task up, task deploy:cloud, ...)
├── kind-config.yaml     # Local kind cluster definition
├── mise.toml            # Pinned tool versions (kubectl, kind, zarf, ...)
├── docs/                # You are here
├── k8s/                 # All Kubernetes manifests (Kustomize)
│   ├── <service>/base + overlays/{local,cloud}/
│   └── main/{local,cloud}/{infra-phase1,infra-phase2,monitoring,opendefense}/
└── zarf/cloud/          # Cloud packaging definition consumed by `task zarf:package:cloud`

Every per-service folder has the same shape: a base/ that knows nothing about the environment, and overlays/<env>/ that layers on the environment-specific bits like hostnames, certificates, and image overrides. See Architecture for the phase composition, and Development Guide for how to work in a service folder.

Glossary

Term Meaning
Rasenmaeher / RM Codename for the Deploy App. Used in image names, env vars, and folder names (e.g. rmapi, rmui).
opendefense Product and brand label for this Kubernetes platform. Most namespaces start with opendefense-.
rmapi / rmui The Rasenmaeher REST API and React UI. The login and onboarding portal.
miniwerk One-shot orchestrator job. Seeds Keycloak, generates certs, and registers the configured products (MW_PRODUCTS).
CFSSL Cloudflare's CA. Used internally for service certificates and mTLS material.
mTLS subdomain Each integrated product has both <product>.<domain> (regular) and mtls.<product>.<domain> (mutual-TLS) hostnames.
Phase Top-level deploy slice: infra-phase1, infra-phase2, monitoring, PVARKI. Applied in order with rollout waits.
Bundle (cloud phase-1) A subfolder under k8s/main/cloud/infra-phase1/bundles/. Rendered into a separate Zarf manifest to stay under Kubernetes Secret size limits.
Local vs cloud local targets a kind cluster on a workstation. cloud targets the k3s VM (k3s-azure.yaml) and ships via Zarf.
Zarf Air-gap-friendly packager. You use Zarf to ship the cloud deployment as one tarball.
